FleetTask.description: One row per ledger entry a developer's fleet has in flight — the grid's live view of _fleet/local/LEDGER.md, projected up before any commit exists.

ActorPresence.description: One row per developer per repo — is their fleet running right now, on which branch, since when. `ended_at` (G3.5, additive) is set on a run_end supersession — the row is never deleted, only re-ingested with `ended_at` populated; a bare SELECT * still returns every version ever ingested (verified — RelataDB has no server-side dedup), so materialize()'s last-write-wins resolution (G3.4) sees the ended state without any row ever being removed. `last_sync` (G8.7, additive) is a DIFFERENT signal than `heartbeat_at`: heartbeat reflects only that the daemon PROCESS is alive (a separate timer in runWatch), while `last_sync` is stamped by daemon.js's syncOnce() only on a cycle that actually completes a full push/pull/materialize round trip — an actor whose cortex connectivity is failing keeps heartbeating (the process is fine) while `last_sync` silently stops advancing, which is exactly the degradation the console's health screen (G8.7) surfaces.

HandoffPointer.description: A pointer to (and a digest of) one handoff file — never the handoff body, never file contents. Server-side cell ACL is not fully wired, so a minimal payload is the defense.

RunEventSummary.description: Per-actor, per-run counts reduced from _fleet/local/runs/<actor>-<ts>/events.jsonl — the run event vocabulary from src/compile/telemetry.js, never the raw event stream itself.

OrgDocument.description: One row per chunk of an imported meeting note, discussion, decision record, or spec (G6.1) — provenance-tracked org knowledge, keyed by content hash so a re-import of unchanged content is a local no-op (RelataDB itself has no server-side dedup on /ingest — see FleetTask's own note — so idempotency here is a client-side digest-tracking concern, the same shape as G3.2's pushed.json). `valid_from` is the document's own business date (the meeting date, not the import date) — a plain data field, not an engine-level bi-temporal parameter; the engine's own system-time versioning is separate, not client-settable, and (verified in G3.3 for every ad-hoc /ingest type on this engine) not even reliably queryable — `_system_from` is a recognized column name whose value is never populated. `imported_at` (G6.5, additive) is therefore a SECOND plain data field, stamped client-side at the moment applyImport() actually calls /ingest — the only honest way to answer 'what had been imported by then' on an engine that cannot answer it itself. `_emb_text` (G6.2, optional) carries the chunk's own text again for the engine/customer-run embedder sidecar to embed on ingest — present only when the sidecar is configured (`RELATA_ACCEL_ENDPOINT`/`accelEndpoint`); recall degrades to BM25 full-text ranking when it is absent. `approval`/`approved_by`/`approved_at` (G7.3, additive) are the org-approved channel's real, first-class approval-lifecycle fields — draft (the default, absent-field state) -> proposed -> approved -> published, enforced client-side by ee/src/grid/approval.js; changing a row's approval state re-ingests the SAME content_hash key with these fields updated, the same bi-temporal-supersession shape ActorPresence.ended_at already established. `rejected_by`/`rejected_at`/`rejection_note` (G8.4, additive) record a proposed->draft send-back: rejection is the one transition that moves BACKWARD, requires a non-empty note (enforced client-side by ee/src/grid/approval.js's rejectOrgDocument), and is real, queryable audit trail (grid audit / explainItem surfaces it), not a side-channel comment.

EquipBinding.description: One row per (fleet, agent, scope_kind, scope_ref) equip decision (G8.5) — which recall purposes, knowledge collections (kind, or kind:client), and procedure sets an agent may draw on. `agent` is '*' for a fleet-wide binding (applies to every agent in that fleet with no more specific row). Consulted by ee/src/memory/relatadb.js's recall() ONLY when a caller passes opts.agent/opts.fleet/opts.repoId — existing callers that never pass those see zero behavior change, and per scope_kind, an ABSENT set of bindings means unrestricted (opt-in restriction, never opt-in permission): recall is byte-identical to pre-G8.5 behavior until a binding is actually written for that repo+fleet+agent+scope_kind.
